3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: The stairway to the Royal Council chambers was longer than I remembered. I took a moment to catch my breath in front of the carved oak doors.

4.speaker: Vina Toras
4.text: "Hurry up, Father! It's not very kingly of you to be late."

8.speaker: Player_Romus
8.text: "A true king is never late. It's the others who are early."

9.speaker: Player_Romus
9.text: "You'd better stop with that when we're inside."

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: After collecting my thoughts, I pushed open the door and walked in.

12.speaker: Narrator
12.text: Everything was just as it had been in my youth. The high domed ceiling, with its skylight that shone into the center of the room. The oval mahogany table. The tall-backed red velvet chair where my father used to sit.

16.speaker: Narrator
16.text: I'd only been here once or twice. I gazed up at the high domed ceiling, with its skylight that shone down into the center of the room. Below it, a tall-backed red velvet chair towered over an oval mahogany table.

17.speaker: Narrator
17.text: When Hugo saw me, he sprang to his feet.

19.speaker: Player_Romus
19.text: "No need to stand on ceremony with me, Hugo. Please sit."

23.speaker: Narrator
23.text: Hugo sat down with a smile.

27.speaker: Hugo Toras
27.text: "Although it seems it won't be as private as I was expecting. Are you staying, Princess Vina?"

28.speaker: Player_Romus
28.text: "Other kings don't have bullet wounds in their legs."

35.speaker: Hugo Toras
35.text: "Rico is still raising hell. But governing Iza has instilled a real sense of responsibility in him. You'd be surprised."

36.speaker: Hugo Toras
36.text: "Busy. Managing the royal transition is a full-time job in itself."

40.speaker: Hugo Toras
40.text: "Rico's still the hellraiser we both know and love. But governing Iza has instilled a real sense of responsibility in him."

41.speaker: Hugo Toras
41.text: "Rita's as much of a thorn in my side as ever. She was begging me to retire after Valero's death."

42.speaker: Narrator
42.text: As I listened to him, my eyes drifted towards the back wall. It was covered in portraits of Rizia's previous kings, including a newly painted likeness of my father.

43.speaker: Hugo Toras
43.text: "My dear brother. I do miss him, but I daresay it's time we had some fresh blood on the throne."

48.speaker: Narrator
48.text: Hugo recognized the formality of my greeting and bowed slightly.

49.speaker: Hugo Toras
49.text: "As Valero never got a chance to fill you in on his royal duties before he passed, I prepared an overview for you. Would you like to hear it?"

53.speaker: Hugo Toras
53.text: "As it's been quite some time since you last sat in these chambers, I've prepared an overview for you. Would you like to hear it?"

57.speaker: Hugo Toras
57.text: "As the king, you're both Rizia's head of state and commander of its armed forces, as well as the de jure governor of Rizia Imperii, Valenqiris, the Pales Administrative District and the island of Caleqabiz."

61.speaker: Player_Romus
61.text: "I'm already up to speed. But I'm sure Vina would appreciate it."

63.speaker: Hugo Toras
63.text: "However, you should not neglect the House of Delegates, the legislative assembly my brother set up to appease the opposition after the uprising."

68.speaker: Hugo Toras
68.text: "His Majesty Valero presided over the last elections in 1949. The Rizian National Coalition secured a House majority, as always."

69.speaker: Hugo Toras
69.text: "I and the rest of the Royal Council will advise you to the best of our ability, and put forth decrees and state decisions for your approval. Ultimately, the King has the final say."

73.speaker: Hugo Toras
73.text: "Thanks to that coronation speech you made, I'd say you're already off on the wrong foot with the RNC."

74.speaker: Hugo Toras
74.text: "Thankfully, your coronation speech got you off on the right foot with the RNC. Even if the speech itself was highly unconventional."
74.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Coronation_Speech_AntiMonarchy"] == true  or  Variable["RiziaDLC.Coronation_Speech_Diplomacy"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Coronation_GaveSpeech"] == true)

78.speaker: Hugo Toras
78.text: "No good can come of ignoring the will of the people."

79.speaker: Player_Romus
79.text: "And if they disagree with me -- so what? I'll have them fired. Or better, beheaded."

80.speaker: Player_Romus
80.text: "Thank you for letting me know. I'll be sure to listen to them going forward."

82.speaker: Hugo Toras
82.text: "The opposition is small but worth keeping an eye on. Especially the new leader, Manus Sazon."

83.speaker: Player_Romus
83.text: "Yes, that was one of his better ideas."

84.speaker: Hugo Toras
84.text: "I thought so as well. It gave Rizia the appearance of a constitutional democracy while keeping power firmly in the hands of the King."

85.speaker: Hugo Toras
85.text: "Shrewd, in fact. It gave Rizia the appearance of a constitutional democracy while keeping power firmly in the hands of the King."

86.speaker: Player_Romus
86.text: "Do the Delegates really represent the will of the people? Or just that of the nobility?"

88.speaker: Narrator
88.text: Hugo scanned my face closely as he spoke the name.

96.speaker: Hugo Toras
96.text: "As you know, Duke Lucas Sazon was executed for his role in your kidnapping and the 1926 uprising, while his wife Angelica was sent into exile on Caleqabiz."

97.speaker: Hugo Toras
97.text: "Upon finishing his studies in Kyrute, Manus returned to the mainland and proceeded to win the largest supporter base of any opposition leader we've seen thus far."

98.speaker: Hugo Toras
98.text: "Then you know he could be a threat."

102.speaker: Player_Romus
102.text: "You're right to be wary of him. We've got to keep him in our sights."

103.speaker: Hugo Toras
103.text: "Yes, that's what makes him particularly dangerous."

104.speaker: Hugo Toras
104.text: "Neither was your father in the '20s, if you'll recall."

119.speaker: Narrator
119.text: He opened a folder and took out a picture of a clean-cut young man. Vina leaned forward to peer at it.

120.speaker: Narrator
120.text: He opened a folder and took out a picture of a clean-cut young man.

121.speaker: Hugo Toras
121.text: "As Grand Vizier, it's traditional for me to attend their sessions and pass any relevant information on to you."

122.speaker: Hugo Toras
122.text: "Keep in mind that Rizia is also a player on the international stage, Your Majesty. We do not have to kowtow to dissenting opinions, but we must tolerate them."

124.speaker: Hugo Toras
124.text: "His promises to give a voice to the common man seem to be resonating with the populace. Part of it, at least."

125.speaker: Hugo Toras
125.text: "Good thinking. This will apply to her too... One day."

129.speaker: Hugo Toras
129.text: "While she remains under strict orders not to leave the island, no such restrictions were placed on the son she gave birth to shortly after her arrival."

130.speaker: Narrator
130.text: To my slight surprise, the room was empty except for one man. My uncle.

131.speaker: Hugo Toras
131.text: "I thought a private chat with your Grand Vizier would be in order before delving into council politics."

132.speaker: Hugo Toras
132.text: "You'll meet everyone else soon enough. But I thought a private chat with your Grand Vizier would be in order first."

133.speaker: Narrator
133.text: His eyes traveled to the doorway, where Vina was still standing.

134.speaker: Vina Toras
134.text: "Yes, Uncle Hugo. I'm sitting in on the King's council meetings."

135.speaker: Narrator
135.text: My daughter gave a shy nod.

136.speaker: Player_Romus
136.text: "I was against the idea, for the record. But she insisted."

137.speaker: Player_Romus
137.text: "She's going to learn by experience, just like I did."

141.speaker: Player_Romus
141.text: "She's going to learn by experience. I wish I had done the same."

142.speaker: Player_Romus
142.text: "It's unorthodox, I know. But future queens should have the same privileges as future kings."

143.speaker: Narrator
143.text: Hugo frowned as he processed this new information, then broke into a smile.

144.speaker: Hugo Toras
144.text: "By all means, then, Your Highness, have a seat."

145.speaker: Narrator
145.text: Vina walked over to the table as I made my way to the red velvet chair. Once we were all seated, I turned to my uncle.

146.speaker: Narrator
146.text: He gestured to the red velvet chair.

147.speaker: Hugo Toras
147.text: "Sila Orica be damned, this is the real seat that matters. And it's been waiting for you."

148.speaker: Narrator
148.text: I made my way over to the chair. Once we were both seated, I turned to my uncle.

149.speaker: Hugo Toras
149.text: "As though I'd trust anyone else to advise my nephew."

151.speaker: Hugo Toras
151.text: "I hope you can make it out for a visit soon. Both of you."

155.speaker: Hugo Toras
155.text: "You and the Princess ought to come out for a visit soon."

156.speaker: Hugo Toras
156.text: "Between that and visits to Rico in Iza, I haven't had a day off since the funeral."

157.speaker: Hugo Toras
157.text: "They propose decrees and issue official approvals or disapprovals of the laws passed by you and the council."

158.speaker: Hugo Toras
158.text: "It still works the way he intended. Rizia has the appearance of a constitutional democracy while power remains firmly in the hands of the King."

161.speaker: Narrator
161.text: Vina finished jotting down some notes as Hugo went searching for the wine.

162.speaker: Hugo Toras
162.text: "I think your father kept a store of vintage Cantuavo in one of these cabinets."

163.speaker: Vina Toras
163.text: "Thank you for the offer anyway, Uncle Hugo."

164.speaker: Vina Toras
164.text: "Thank you for the invitation, Uncle Hugo."

166.speaker: Player_Romus
166.text: "Gladly. We still have much to catch up on."

169.speaker: Player_Romus
169.text: "I'm your superior now, Your Grace. It wouldn't be appropriate."

170.speaker: Narrator
170.text: Hugo scowled briefly, then forced a smile.

172.speaker: Hugo Toras
172.text: "Noon already. Shall we and the young heiress break for a glass of wine before the council convenes this afternoon?"

178.speaker: Player_Romus
178.text: "I could never stand the taste of alcohol."

183.speaker: Player_Romus
183.text: "I overdid it as the Party Prince. I'm clean now."

187.speaker: Player_Romus
187.text: "I don't remember. I just stopped at some point."

188.speaker: Hugo Toras
188.text: "A respectable decision. But on the other hand..."

189.speaker: Hugo Toras
189.text: "A curious way of expressing your devotion. Alcohol consumption is expressly permitted in most Nurist denominations."

191.speaker: Hugo Toras
191.text: "You should remember that it's highly untraditional for a Rizian monarch to refuse his country's national beverage."

194.speaker: Narrator
194.text: He stood up, then paused and turned back to me.

195.speaker: Hugo Toras
195.text: "I think your father kept a store of vintage Cantuavo in one of these cabinets."

197.speaker: Player_Romus
197.text: "Gladly. We still have much to catch up on."

199.speaker: Player_Romus
199.text: "I'm your superior now, Your Grace. It wouldn't be appropriate."

200.speaker: Narrator
200.text: Hugo scowled, then forced a smile.

202.speaker: Hugo Toras
202.text: "Noon already. Shall we break for a glass of wine before the council convenes this afternoon?"

204.speaker: Narrator
204.text: He stood up, then paused and turned back to me.

209.speaker: Player_Romus
209.text: "I overdid it as the Party Prince. I'm clean now."

213.speaker: Player_Romus
213.text: "I don't remember. I just stopped at some point."

215.speaker: Hugo Toras
215.text: "That's an extreme interpretation of Wruhecism. But I can respect it."

218.speaker: Player_Romus
218.text: "I could never stand the taste of alcohol."

219.speaker: Hugo Toras
219.text: "You should find a way to keep this a secret, though. No Rizian monarch can be seen refusing his country's national beverage."

220.speaker: Player_Romus
220.text: "Oh. Well, in that case, my sober days are over. Pour me a glass."

224.speaker: Player_Romus
224.text: "If tradition demands it, you might as well pour me a glass."

225.speaker: Player_Romus
225.text: "Duly noted, but this isn't a formal occasion. I respectfully decline."

227.speaker: Vina Toras
227.text: "Thank you for the offer anyway, Uncle Hugo."

229.speaker: Hugo Toras
229.text: "I know how overwhelming the move to the capital can be, Your Highness. If you ever need someone to talk to, remember you can always come to me."

230.speaker: Narrator
230.text: He turned to look Vina in the eye.

232.speaker: Vina Toras
232.text: "That's very kind of you, Uncle Hugo."

233.speaker: Narrator
233.text: He turned to look my daughter in the eye.

234.speaker: Hugo Toras
234.text: "What an intelligent and well-mannered young woman you've grown up to be, Your Highness."

235.speaker: Hugo Toras
235.text: "I know how overwhelming the capital can seem compared to Monqiz. If you ever have questions, don't be afraid to come to me."

237.speaker: Vina Toras
237.text: "That's very kind of you, Uncle Hugo."

239.speaker: Player_Romus
239.text: "Listen to your uncle, Vina. He knows how everything works around here."

241.speaker: Hugo Toras
241.text: "Forgive my forwardness. I'm simply excited to have the family together again."

242.speaker: Hugo Toras
242.text: "What is my role as Grand Vizier, if not to advise the royal family?"

243.speaker: Hugo Toras
243.text: "I said it all to you during our hunting days, Romus."

247.speaker: Hugo Toras
247.text: "The larger your quarry, the more important it is not to miss."

248.speaker: Narrator
248.text: Vina finished jotting down a few notes. The three of us packed up and left for the morning.

249.speaker: Hugo Toras
249.text: "I wouldn't presume to know better than you, Your Majesty."

250.speaker: Hugo Toras
250.text: "But of course you can always come to me with questions as well."

252.speaker: Player_Romus
252.text: "Listen to your uncle, Vina. He knows how everything works around here."

254.speaker: Hugo Toras
254.text: "Pardon my forwardness. I'm simply excited to have the family together again."

255.speaker: Hugo Toras
255.text: "What is my role as Grand Vizier, if not to advise the royal family?"

256.speaker: Hugo Toras
256.text: "I said it all to you during our hunting days, Romus."

257.speaker: Hugo Toras
257.text: "I wouldn't presume to know better than you, Your Majesty."

261.speaker: Hugo Toras
261.text: "The more ferocious your quarry, the more important it is not to miss."

262.speaker: Hugo Toras
262.text: "But of course you can always come to me with questions as well."

263.speaker: Hugo Toras
263.text: "I hope young Vina is adjusting to life in the capital? Please let her know that if she has questions, she shouldn't feel shy about coming to me."

264.speaker: Hugo Toras
264.text: "I hope young Vina is adjusting to life in the capital? Please let her know that if she has questions, she shouldn't feel shy about coming to me."

266.speaker: Player_Romus
266.text: "Thank you for the offer. I'll let her know."

268.speaker: Narrator
268.text: He turned away and started searching for the wine.

269.speaker: Hugo Toras
269.text: "Forgive my forwardness. I'm simply excited to have the family together again."

270.speaker: Hugo Toras
270.text: "What is my role as Grand Vizier, if not to advise the royal family?"

271.speaker: Hugo Toras
271.text: "I said it all to you during our hunting days, Romus."

272.speaker: Hugo Toras
272.text: "I wouldn't presume to know better than you, Your Majesty."

276.speaker: Hugo Toras
276.text: "The more ferocious your quarry, the more important it is not to miss."

277.speaker: Hugo Toras
277.text: "But of course you can always come to me with questions as well."

279.speaker: Player_Romus
279.text: "Thank you for the offer. I'll let her know."

281.speaker: Narrator
281.text: He turned away. The two of us packed up in silence and left for the morning.

282.speaker: Hugo Toras
282.text: "Forgive my forwardness. I'm simply excited to have the family together again."

283.speaker: Hugo Toras
283.text: "What is my role as Grand Vizier, if not to advise the royal family?"

284.speaker: Hugo Toras
284.text: "I said it all to you during our hunting days, Romus."

285.speaker: Hugo Toras
285.text: "I wouldn't presume to know better than you, Your Majesty."

289.speaker: Hugo Toras
289.text: "The larger your quarry, the more important it is not to miss."

290.speaker: Hugo Toras
290.text: "But of course you can always come to me with questions as well."

292.speaker: Player_Romus
292.text: "Why can't I attend? I want to be in touch with my populace."

293.speaker: Player_Romus
293.text: "What do you think would be the consequences if I ignore them?"

294.speaker: Hugo Toras
294.text: "Officially, there are none. Unofficially, I'd advise you to take their input into account."

295.speaker: Hugo Toras
295.text: "The sessions can be quite long and tedious, Your Majesty. The King's time is better spent on other matters."

296.speaker: Hugo Toras
296.text: "With that said, I would advise you to take the Delegates' input into account."

297.speaker: Hugo Toras
297.text: "Fortunately, the Delegates' speaker, Daria de Rava, is a Toras loyalist through and through. She should give you no trouble."

299.speaker: Player_Romus
299.text: "I don't need all this. I can fend for myself."

300.speaker: Player_Romus
300.text: "So they're guarding Vina and Queen Mother Estela as well?"

304.speaker: Titus Gordion
304.text: "Your limp says otherwise. There's no way that would have happened on our watch."

305.speaker: Titus Gordion
305.text: "What about your young daughter? Your elderly mother? It may not always be you that your enemies target."

306.speaker: Titus Gordion
306.text: "Yes, my men have eyes on both of them as we speak."

307.speaker: Hugo Toras
307.text: "One more thing. As you're aware, a few years before your father's death, he reinstated the Golden Guard..."

308.speaker: Player_Romus
308.text: "Right. The royal family's personal security force. And where are they now?"

312.speaker: Narrator
312.text: For the first time, I noticed the man standing in the corner of the room. He was wearing a tight-fitting gold blazer that barely concealed his muscular physique.

313.speaker: Hugo Toras
313.text: "Meet Titus Gordion, captain of the Golden Guard. He and his men have been keeping a close watch on you since the coronation."

314.speaker: Titus Gordion
314.text: "We hope to serve you well, sir."

315.speaker: Titus Gordion
315.text: "For his and your personal protection, sir."

316.speaker: Titus Gordion
316.text: "A Golden Guard appears only if and when he is needed, sir."

318.speaker: Player_Romus
318.text: "Has he been in the room with us this whole time?"

319.speaker: Player_Romus
319.text: "I'm pleased to meet you, Captain Gordion."

321.speaker: Hugo Toras
321.text: "Titus and the members of his two-thousand strong brigade have been trained in the upper echelons of Rizia's military and police academies. Each has sworn an oath to protect the King and his family at all costs."

322.speaker: Titus Gordion
322.text: "My apologies, sir. I was waiting for an opportune time to introduce myself."

326.speaker: Titus Gordion
326.text: "Yes. My men have eyes on the Queen Mother as we speak."

327.speaker: Narrator
327.text: He bowed to Vina. She looked a little flustered.

328.speaker: Vina Toras
328.text: "But didn't Queen Lyza discontinue the Golden Guard? Because she thought they made royals look elitist, and because..."

330.speaker: Titus Gordion
330.text: "Because she thought they were getting too powerful. It's why our current force is less than a fifth of the size it once was."

334.speaker: Player_Romus
334.text: "What's with the costumes? Wouldn't plainclothes bodyguards be more effective?"

335.speaker: Titus Gordion
335.text: "It sends the signal that you are well protected, sir. My predecessors wore solid gold breastplates."

336.speaker: Player_Romus
336.text: "And how do we know they can be trusted? What if someone gets to them?"

337.speaker: Titus Gordion
337.text: "I conduct regular screenings of each and every member of my brigade, Your Majesty. As for myself, I have no wife and child to threaten, and I receive a paycheck so large that bribery would be of no use."

338.speaker: Hugo Toras
338.text: "Your father always had a fondness for Rizian tradition. So he spared no expense in bringing the Guard back, albeit in a reduced form."

339.speaker: Hugo Toras
339.text: "My mother Lyza discontinued the Golden Guard. But King Valero always did have a fondness for Rizian tradition. He spared no expense in bringing it back."

340.speaker: Player_Romus
340.text: "You and your men had better stay in line, Captain Gordion."

341.speaker: Player_Romus
341.text: "It humbles me to be worthy of such an elite unit's protection."

342.speaker: Player_Romus
342.text: "He was right to do so. The most important family in Rizia deserves the most important security force."

343.speaker: Player_Romus
343.text: "Guards in gold... it still seems too flashy for me."

344.speaker: Titus Gordion
344.text: "We'll be sure to stay out of your way, sir."

347.speaker: Titus Gordion
347.text: "We answer to no one but you, sir."

348.speaker: Hugo Toras
348.text: "Thank you, Titus. You may wait outside the chambers until the meeting's conclusion."

350.speaker: Narrator
350.text: Titus nodded and swiftly left the room.

353.speaker: Player_Romus
353.text: "Sounds like a waste of time. I'd rather just make all the decrees myself."

354.speaker: Hugo Toras
354.text: "I'd advise you to at least take the Delegates' input into account, Your Majesty."

355.speaker: Player_Romus
355.text: "You're wrong. It is very kingly of me to show up whenever I want."

356.speaker: Player_Romus
356.text: "Thanks for that, Your Grace. I will be counting on you."

358.speaker: Player_Romus
358.text: "Great. Looking forward to working with them."

360.speaker: Hugo Toras
360.text: "It was the only way for him to stay in power. Rizia could not survive past the 1920s without some semblance of democracy."

363.speaker: Hugo Toras
363.text: "Do not discount the importance of the nobility to this kingdom, my nephew. Keep them satisfied, and commoners' lives will be better for it."

364.speaker: Hugo Toras
364.text: "But if you want a self-styled 'man of the people', look no further than the opposition."

365.speaker: Hugo Toras
365.text: "More specifically, to their new leader Manus Sazon."

372.speaker: Hugo Toras
372.text: "Like your father and grandmother before you, you alone have the power to shape this country by passing royal decrees."

373.speaker: Hugo Toras
373.text: "As is tradition over hundreds of years, each new ruler has passed the Sovereign Transition and Clemency Decree to start their reign."

374.speaker: Hugo Toras
374.text: "The kingdom will be expecting your decree very soon."

375.speaker: Player_Romus
375.text: "I would never go against the traditions of Rizia. I will sign the decree as soon as possible."

376.speaker: Player_Romus
376.text: "The decrees will play a significant role in my reign. They won't be just symbolic gestures, but tools to shape the future of Rizia."

377.speaker: Player_Romus
377.text: "Thanks for your advice, uncle. It's comforting to have your wisdom and experience guiding me at the start of my reign."

378.speaker: Hugo Toras
378.text: "Your humility is appreciated. But remember, being King is about making hard decisions, not just following advice."

379.speaker: Hugo Toras
379.text: "Wield this power wisely, Romus. The decrees you issue should strengthen the fabric of our kingdom, not tear it."

380.speaker: Hugo Toras
380.text: "Very good. Upholding tradition is key to the stability of our monarchy and the continued loyalty of our people."

384.speaker: Player_Romus
384.text: "I've been looking forward to this all my life. Finally, I have the power to make decisions completely unchallenged."

386.speaker: Player_Romus
386.text: "Tradition is the enemy of progress. We should not be bound by the past."

387.speaker: Hugo Toras
387.text: "Disregarding tradition is a perilous path, Romus. Our people cherish these customs. They are the bedrock of our society."

388.speaker: Hugo Toras
388.text: "I still urge caution. Nobody can stop you from passing decrees, but you have to be prepared for possible backlash."

389.speaker: Hugo Toras
389.text: "Moving too swiftly away from them -- as you did during your coronation --might bring unrest."

393.speaker: Narrator
393.text: Hugo reached for a neatly rolled parchment lying on the grand table. With deliberate movements, he unrolled it, revealing the prepared royal decree.

394.speaker: Narrator
394.text: The intricate script and the seal of Rizia glinted under the chandelier's light.

400.speaker: Player_Romus
400.text: "It troubles me that a single person can hold that much power. I am as fallible as anyone else."

401.speaker: Hugo Toras
401.text: "That's what your advisors are for, my nephew."

402.speaker: Hugo Toras
402.text: "I will, however, gently remind you that it is traditional for each new monarch of Rizia to pass the Sovereign Transition and Clemency Decree to start their reign."

403.speaker: Hugo Toras
403.text: "The kingdom will be expecting your signature soon."

407.speaker: Hugo Toras
407.text: "You were assisting with royal decrees before your reign. Now, you're the one holding the seal."

408.speaker: Hugo Toras
408.text: "I think we're almost done here. Unless there's anything else you'd like to bring up?"

414.speaker: Player_Romus
414.text: "It troubles me that a single person can hold that much power. I am as fallible as anyone else."

415.speaker: Hugo Toras
415.text: "Moving too swiftly away from them -- as you did during your coronation --might bring unrest."

416.speaker: Hugo Toras
416.text: "That's what your advisors are for, my nephew."

423.speaker: Player_Romus
423.text: "I would never go against the traditions of Rizia. I will sign the decree as soon as possible."

424.speaker: Hugo Toras
424.text: "I urge you to reconsider, Romus. No monarch wants to be remembered as a tyrant."

425.speaker: Hugo Toras
425.text: "Very good. Upholding tradition is key to the stability of our monarchy and the continued loyalty of our people."

426.speaker: Player_Romus
426.text: "I've been looking forward to this all my life. Finally, the power to make decisions completely unchallenged."

427.speaker: Player_Romus
427.text: "Tradition is the enemy of progress. We should not be bound by the past."

428.speaker: Hugo Toras
428.text: "Disregarding tradition is a perilous path, Romus. Our people cherish these customs. They are the bedrock of our society."

429.speaker: Hugo Toras
429.text: "I still urge caution. Nobody can stop you from passing decrees, but you have to be prepared for possible backlash."

430.speaker: Player_Romus
430.text: "Clemency? Ha! Under me, the people of Rizia will know no clemency."

435.speaker: Hugo Toras
435.text: "At any rate, since you say you're caught up on the political situation, the rest of our meeting won't last long. But perhaps you'd appreciate an update on the noble houses."
